subject: Runauto function with locally downloaded NCEP files

messages.author: a236684e6b11c6fa
messages.subject: Runauto function with locally downloaded NCEP files
parts:
Hi everyone, 
I have just downloaded and reordered the NCEP files as already suggested in this group.
There is an option for micro_ncep to read these local files. I am wondering if this is also possible with rhe runauto function? 
How can I tell the runauto function to use the locally stored NCEP files? 
Any help is greatly appreciated.
Best regards
Felix

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Runauto function with locally downloaded NCEP files
parts:
Hi Felix,

If you make your own version of runauto and change the line:

    micronmr <- micro_ncep(dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish,
        dem = r, dem2 = dem, LAI = 0, loc = loc, Usrhyt = hgt2,
        Refhyt = 2, coastal = coastal, reanalysis = reanalysis2,
        DEP = dep, save = save, hourlydata = hourlydata, dailyprecip = dailyprecip,
        weather.elev = weather.elev, cad.effects = cad.effects)

to

    micronmr <- micro_ncep(dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish,
        dem = r, dem2 = dem, LAI = 0, loc = loc, Usrhyt = hgt2,
        Refhyt = 2, coastal = coastal, reanalysis = reanalysis2,
        DEP = dep, save = save, hourlydata = hourlydata, dailyprecip = dailyprecip,
        weather.elev = weather.elev, cad.effects = cad.effects, spatial = 'your ncep data location')

I think it will work.

All the best,
Mike

Is it possible to keep the runauto function or was your suggestion to use the micro_ncep function instead and transform it?

Hi Felix and Mike,

From some of my troubleshooting with these functions, perhaps this may provide a lead of where the issue/bug is in the code: that error suggests that at some point a vector was made completely NA, before being handed to a logical statement-- the error itself is thrown by the logical statement, and in my experience from troubleshooting microclima, the vector was made NA when the mean() is taken of an upstream vector that has at least one NA. As an example, see this line 1087 on the micro_ncep() function: in this line, if there are any NAs in the vector `VPD_diff`, then mean(VPD_diff) will just return NA, which will make VPDhr also NA, and so on.

So Felix, you might want to check if there are any NA values in any of your data inputs. Mike, in some of Ilya's functions I've added an argument `na.rm = TRUE` to any uses of mean(), min(), max(), and sometimes an informative error of "found NAs in vector X", as ways to prevent or trap this error. But I haven't had the chance to pull request any such changes to NicheMapR functions.

Best,
Dave
